thread:
samira: FYI customer AcmeApp is seeing p99 regressions on streaming endpoints vs non-streaming. They say streaming TTFB spikes to 700-1200ms on some requests while synchronous returns in ~200-300ms. Filing here before escalating to runtime.

samira: Customer provided a couple of recordings and their repro. Key symptom: first chunk arrives fast for some requests but for many others we send a very small first chunk (~8-20 bytes) then nothing for 600-800ms, then the rest flows. Non-streaming total time is lower.

samira: Repro steps they gave:
```bash
# streaming (server-sent events / chunked)
curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=open-rl"

# non-streaming
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=open-rl"
```

samira: Customer also captured a tcpdump and a trace from our SDK; attaching snippets below.

samira: tcpdump snippet (abbreviated):
```
... TLS record, application data, first chunk 14 bytes ...
... NO APPLICATION DATA for 742 ms ...
... TLS record, application data, follow-up chunk 3.2KB ...
```

devon: Thanks, Samira. Can you paste the request payload sizes and model? small prompts? streaming frequency?

samira: Prompt sizes are small (single-paragraph prompts), model open-rl (65B context), streaming tokens often come 1-3 tokens at first. They use HTTP/2 via our public edge (customer based in EU region).

josh: Interesting — this looks like classic small-first-chunk + proxy buffering. We've seen HTTP/2/window + upstream proxy (nginx/traefik) delay flush until a certain threshold or until the flow-control window opens. Also client-side handling of tiny chunks can add head-of-line if the connection multiplexing reorders streams.

eng-rtg-bot: Trace uploaded: span[root] -> span[response_writer.wait_for_flush] shows 580ms wait between write() returning and socket FIN for first real content.

maria: Did the customer try with `Accept: text/event-stream` vs `application/json; charset=utf-8` streaming? Some clients treat SSE differently.

samira: They tried both; behavior consistent. Also reproduced with raw `--no-buffer` curl and with our Python SDK streaming iterator.

kyle: Can you paste the runtime logs for that request id? I want to see how we flush in the runtime.

samira: Pasted below (redacted):
```
[2026-02-15T10:12:34.123Z] request_id=rc-12345 write_chunk size=14 wrote_bytes=14 flush=true
[2026-02-15T10:12:34.127Z] request_id=rc-12345 sleep 0.003s loop
[2026-02-15T10:12:35.003Z] request_id=rc-12345 write_chunk size=3278 wrote_bytes=3278 flush=true
```

kyle: So runtime is issuing flushes immediately for the small chunk. That suggests the server is not coalescing client-side. The edge or proxy likely coalesces or stalls tiny initial frames.

josh: I want to rule out TCP Nagle interactions but since connections are TLS and chunking, it's more likely HTTP/2 frame/windowing.

maria: Short-term mitigation options for the customer:
- Force non-streaming (they said it's slightly faster for their p99) by using the sync endpoint as a workaround.
- Increase the initial flushed token size via the SDK (coalesce tokens before first write) — we can suggest a client change.
- Use our dedicated connection (Dedicated or Private) to bypass the public edge for customers on reserved capacity.

samira: Customer prefers we fix on our side. They asked for an ETA.

josh: Proposed short-term runtime patch: coalesce outgoing streaming data until either (a) accumulated bytes >= 256 bytes OR (b) wall-clock time since first token >= 120ms, then flush. This reduces tiny-first-chunk cases while still preserving streaming for longer outputs.

maria: That sounds reasonable. Any risk of increased latency for small very-latent tokens? We need to ensure we don't add 120ms to everyone. Maybe make threshold 100ms + adaptive if downstream detects H2 backpressure.

kyle: Implementation notes: runtime write path currently calls flush per token by default to minimize latency. We can implement a configurable coalesce window per customer. Add metrics for "coalesce_delay_ms" and "initial_chunk_size".

sre-jen: From SRE perspective, a config flag is ideal so we can enable per-tenant and canary. Also want to ensure this doesn't increase memory usage significantly. Canary on 5% of traffic for EU edge first.

eng-rtg-bot: Created ticket INF-1983: "runtime: initial-stream-chunk coalescing + per-tenant config" (link: https://redwood.internal/INF-1983).

deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: runtime v2.14.0-canary -> eu-edge (5%) at 2026-02-18T02:00Z.

devon: Owner for the patch? Josh for runtime change? Maria for SDK guidance? Samira to coordinate customer comms?

josh: I'll take the runtime PR. Plan: prototype coalesce buffer + metrics -> unit tests for latency regression -> canary. Est ETA: 3 business days for prototype, 1-2 days for tests and code review, then canary.

maria: I'll craft a recommended client-side snippet we can send meanwhile:
```python
# Python SDK pseudo: coalesce before yielding first chunk
buf = []
for token in model.stream_tokens(prompt):
    buf.append(token)
    if len(''.join(buf)) >= 200 or (time.time() - start) > 0.08:
        yield ''.join(buf)
        buf = []
```

samira: I'll tell AcmeApp: short-term options + we will run a canary of a runtime change next week. Ask them to try sync endpoint until canary completes.

sre-jen: Also recommend we add an observability check: detect requests where initial_chunk_size < 64 bytes and initial_chunk_gap > 200ms and add alert to paging threshold (or runbook).

kyle: I'll add the metrics to the runtime PR and a dashboard showing p50/p95/p99 TTFB for streaming vs non-streaming per region.

samira: Thanks all. Action items:
- josh -> RFC + PR for INF-1983 (coalescing) (owner)
- kyle -> add metrics + dashboard
- maria -> prepare client-side snippet + comms
- samira -> update customer and capture their confirmation
- sre-jen -> add canary gating and runbook updates

samira: I'll post updates here as we progress.

kyle: Noted. Also tagging @eng-security in case any header/control-plane changes needed for per-tenant config.

maria: FYI adding a feature flag per-tenant requires config plumbing; I can scope that in the PR or as a follow-up depending on timeline.

samira: Closing loop for now. If anyone runs into blocking infra (canary infra) ping me.

josh: Starting the prototype now. Will link PR in this thread when ready.

eng-rtg-bot: PR linked: https://redwood.internal/pull/4321 (runtime coalesce prototype)

samira: Great — keeping AcmeApp in the loop.
